description: The line plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing, measured as accuracy (ACC %) on the y-axis, across different editing methods applied to LLMs, as a function of co-occurrence number on the x-axis, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴. The y-axis spans from 60% to 80% ACC, with major gridlines at 5% intervals. Six distinct editing methods are compared: “Base” (black solid line with circle markers), “MEND” (brown solid line with diamond markers), “FT” (blue solid line with downward triangle markers), “MEMIT” (purple solid line with pentagon markers), “IKE” (red solid line with upward triangle markers), and “ROME” (green solid line with square markers). All lines show a generally increasing trend in accuracy as co-occurrence number increases. At the lowest co-occurrence (near 1), “Base” starts at ~63%, “FT” at ~64%, “IKE” at ~66%, “MEMIT” at ~68%, “MEND” at ~69%, and “ROME” at ~73%. At the highest co-occurrence (~10⁴), “Base” reaches ~69%, “FT” ~70.5%, “IKE” ~72.5%, “MEMIT” ~75%, “MEND” ~77%, and “ROME” peaks at ~81%. “ROME” consistently outperforms all other methods across the entire range, while “Base” remains the lowest-performing method throughout.
